knowledge:
- key_parameters: df=The input dataset, which can be a SummarizedExperiment object or a matrix-like R data structure (e.g., matrix, data frame) ;; classes=A character vector containing sample class labels, where the quality control sample class must be labeled as "QC" ;; method (in filter_peaks_by_fraction)=Determines the filtering approach, either "QC" to filter based on QC samples only, or "across" to filter across all samples ;; method (in mv_imputation)=The imputation algorithm to use, supporting "knn", "rf", "bpca", "mean", "median", or "mn" (constant small value) ;; order (in QCRSC)=A numeric vector containing the sample injection order during analytical measurement ;; batch (in QCRSC)=A numeric or character vector containing sample batch identifiers ;; minQC (in QCRSC)=The minimum number of QC samples required per batch for spline fitting (recommended to be at least 4)
- alternatives: xcms=Mentioned as a raw data processing package used to perform peak picking and generate the initial peak matrix before using pmp
- when_to_use: Appropriate for untargeted metabolomics datasets (such as direct infusion mass spectrometry or liquid chromatography mass spectrometry peak tables) to remove uninformative or irreproducible features, normalize signals, impute missing values, and correct for batch effects and signal drift prior to downstream statistical analysis.
- pitfalls: Missing values are not supported by the smoothed spline regression in the QC-RSC algorithm, so features with high missingness must be filtered out first or imputed ;; Spline fitting requires a minimum number of QC samples per batch (at least 4 QC values are recommended) to be reliable ;; If using matrix-like inputs instead of SummarizedExperiment, the package automatically transposes the matrix to have features as rows and samples as columns, which may trigger warnings if class labels are missing.

workflows.name: metabolomics_filtering_and_normalization
workflows.intent: Filter, normalize, impute, and scale a metabolomics peak matrix to prepare it for downstream statistical analysis.
input: MTBLS79 (SummarizedExperiment object containing metabolomics peak matrix and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter samples by missing value percentage using filter_samples_by_mv ;; 2. Filter peaks by fraction of missing values in QC samples using filter_peaks_by_fraction ;; 3. Filter peaks by fraction of missing values across all samples using filter_peaks_by_fraction ;; 4. Filter peaks by relative standard deviation (RSD) in QC samples using filter_peaks_by_rsd ;; 5. Track processing history using processing_history ;; 6. Normalize data using probabilistic quotient normalization with pqn_normalisation ;; 7. Impute missing values using mv_imputation ;; 8. Perform generalized logarithm transformation using glog_transformation ;; 9. Plot optimized lambda for glog transformation using glog_plot_optimised_lambda
workflows.code:
MTBLS79_filtered <- filter_samples_by_mv(df=MTBLS79, max_perc_mv=0.1)
MTBLS79_filtered <- filter_peaks_by_fraction(df=MTBLS79_filtered, min_frac=0.9, classes=MTBLS79_filtered$Class, method="QC", qc_label="QC")
MTBLS79_filtered <- filter_peaks_by_fraction(df=MTBLS79_filtered, min_frac=0.9, classes=MTBLS79_filtered$Class, method="across")
MTBLS79_filtered <- filter_peaks_by_rsd(df=MTBLS79_filtered, max_rsd=30, classes=MTBLS79_filtered$Class, qc_label="QC")
processing_history(MTBLS79_filtered)
MTBLS79_pqn_normalised <- pqn_normalisation(df=MTBLS79_filtered, classes=MTBLS79_filtered$Class, qc_label="QC")
MTBLS79_mv_imputed <- mv_imputation(df=MTBLS79_pqn_normalised, method="knn")
MTBLS79_glog <- glog_transformation(df=MTBLS79_mv_imputed, classes=MTBLS79_filtered$Class, qc_label="QC")
opt_lambda <- processing_history(MTBLS79_glog)$glog_transformation$lambda_opt
glog_plot_optimised_lambda(df=MTBLS79_mv_imputed, optimised_lambda=opt_lambda, classes=MTBLS79_filtered$Class, qc_label="QC")

workflows.name: signal_drift_and_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Correct signal drift and batch effects across multi-batch mass spectrometry datasets using Quality Control-Robust Spline Correction (QC-RSC).
input: MTBLS79 (SummarizedExperiment object containing metabolomics peak matrix and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out peaks not reproducibly measured across QC samples using filter_peaks_by_fraction ;; 2. Apply signal drift and batch effect correction using QCRSC ;; 3. Visually compare results before and after correction using sbc_plot
workflows.code:
class <- MTBLS79$Class
batch <- MTBLS79$Batch
sample_order <- c(1:ncol(MTBLS79))
data <- filter_peaks_by_fraction(df=MTBLS79, classes=class, method="QC", qc_label="QC", min_frac=0.8)
corrected_data <- QCRSC(df=data, order=sample_order, batch=batch, classes=class, spar=0, minQC=4)
plots <- sbc_plot (df=MTBLS79, corrected_df=corrected_data, classes=class, batch=batch, output=NULL, indexes=c(1, 5, 30))
